_: The declared cost dependencies of every product, machine-readable.
This file answers one question the prose ledger could not: for a given
product, what does it cost to keep it alive? Two halves make that up —
`subscriptions`, which are fixed and per-product, and `pools`, which are
shared resources several products draw on and where the per-product number
has to be attributed rather than read off a bill.
`source` on every subscription says where the number came from. Nothing here
is a billing-API reading; they are hand-entered from the record named. Treat
each as last-known-state and re-verify before acting on it.
Edit this file, not the prose. `01-Knowledge Base/Infrastructure Ledger.md`
Part 2 is GENERATED from it by `ledger.py render` — hand-editing the prose
is how it went stale for three weeks while every fact around it moved.
`keys` names the LABEL in ledger/keys.md, never a value. keys.py is
the only thing that reads that file; nothing here or in the prose

openrouter.label: OpenRouter
openrouter.billing: prepaid credit, drawn down by usage
openrouter.note: One balance, several products. Exact per-product spend needs one API key per product plus a management key to read /api/v1/activity?api_key_hash=. Until that exists, attribution falls back to what each project recorded itself in Costs.jsonl, and the difference from the pool total is reported as unattributed rather than spread.

known_non_product_keys.MCP: OpenRouter MCP: Claude: Auto-created by OpenRouter when the connector was added to Claude Code, 2026-08-20. $0.000 used because the connector's reads (credits, models, docs) are free. EXPIRES 2026-08-27 — the connector stops working that day unless renewed. Leave it alone; it is not a product key. But if the connector is ever used to GENERATE (send-message, generate-image), that spend bills here and will show as unattributed, so check this row before blaming a product. The expiry CANNOT be removed or extended: it is set when the OAuth flow mints the key, and PATCH /keys/{hash} accepts name, limit, limit_reset and disabled but has no expires_at field. OpenRouter's MCP server (mcp.openrouter.ai/mcp) only supports OAuth, not API-key headers, so there is no permanent-connection variant. Re-auth with `claude mcp login openrouter` — one command, config is preserved. Nothing in the ledger depends on it: the balance is read with the `management` key, which never expires.
known_non_product_keys.Default key: RETIRED 2026-08-20 by the owner. The original shared key: $25.27 drawn across four products, which is the entire unattributed balance and always will be — deleting the key does not recover attribution, and OpenRouter's activity history only reaches back 30 days. Its $25.27 stays in the account total and is the permanent cost of having started with one key. Two projects were still reading it when it died: gamma (code/site/secrets.json, H-024) and alpha (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, H-025).

openrouter.attribution_baseline: 2026-08-20: per-product keys issued. Everything drawn BEFORE this date is unattributable by construction; everything after is attributable by key. Do not try to reconcile the $25.27 — treat it as opening balance.

alpha.note: documents and pipeline, no hosting. Four launchd agents run unattended on this Mac (sweep and evaluate every 6h, prepare daily, replies every 30min) and `evaluate` is the spending one: `openrouter-runner.mjs pipeline` scores every pending role, measured 2026-08-21 at $0.0033 a role. The key label was missing here until 2026-08-21, so its spend was counted as a non-product key and never named in `reconcile`.

delta.note: GitHub, plus opt-in routed inference for measurement runs
delta.pool_note: The synthesis layer and the funnel run on a local model by default and cost nothing. From 2026-08-22 they can be routed through delta's proxy onto this pool by setting MIKOSHI_LLM_BASE_URL — opt-in per run, never a default, because switching to a paid route is a money decision. First such run the same day: $0.062 for a 30-question quality eval.
